problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & 6 \\ 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 9 & 6 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 9 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(-1-\lambda )-9) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda -8) & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)^{2}(\lambda +4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=-4.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{-4}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{2}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-2I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & 6 \\ 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-3 & 9 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$ So,

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{2})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-4})+\text{dim}({V}_{2})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, a corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$
